_meta.indication: Treatment of chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) after failure of at least two prior lines of systemic therapy in adult and pediatric patients weighing at least 40 kg.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1:1), open-label, multicenter study evaluating axatilimab-csfr at three dose levels (0.3 mg/kg IV Q2W, 1 mg/kg IV Q2W, or 3 mg/kg IV Q4W); the 0.3 mg/kg Q2W cohort was the efficacy analysis cohort.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and pediatric patients with recurrent or refractory cGVHD who had received at least 2 lines of systemic therapy and required additional treatment.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (complete or partial response) per 2014 NIH consensus criteria within the first 6 cycles of therapy.
pivotal_trials.n: Efficacy cohort N=79 (axatilimab-csfr 0.3 mg/kg IV Q2W)
pivotal_trials.result: ORR through Cycle 7 Day 1 of 75% (95% CI 64, 84); all responses were PR. Median time to first response 1.5 months; no death or new systemic therapy in 60% (95% CI 43, 74) of responders for at least 12 months. At least a 7-point decrease in modified Lee Symptom Scale in 56% (95% CI 44, 67).

key_safety: Most common (≥15%) adverse reactions were increased AST, infection (pathogen unspecified), increased ALT, decreased phosphate, decreased hemoglobin, viral infection, increased GGT, and others. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 44% of patients (infection, viral infection, respiratory failure). Infusion-related reactions occurred in 18% (Grade 3-4 in 1.3%).
target_moa: Axatilimab is a colony stimulating factor-1 receptor (CSF-1R)-blocking antibody. CSF-1R is a receptor tyrosine kinase that binds its ligand CSF-1; in vitro axatilimab inhibited MCP-1 release by macrophages and CSF-1R internalization and activation.
modality: mAb — humanized IgG4 (kappa light chain) monoclonal antibody

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not discussed by an Advisory Committee, because there were no efficacy or safety issues identified for discussion.
